articles.title: Shedeur Sanders' Brother Shilo Calls Out Browns Reporters for 'Messy' Questions to QB in New Video
articles.summary: Shilo Sanders, the brother of Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders, posted a video criticizing reporters for their "messy questions" while watching his brother's Wednesday press conference.
articles.body:
Shilo Sanders, the brother of Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders, posted a video criticizing reporters for their "messy questions" while watching his brother's Wednesday press conference.

"He handled that interview really good," Shilo said. "They try to get him caught up in stuff, and he's good at just keeping the main thing the main thing, and just focusing on what's important, and that's winning games and doing your job. So that was a great interview by Shedeur."

Sanders has served as the backup quarterback through the early portion of the 2026 season, but he is expected to make his first start of the season against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. He's likely to step in for starting quarterback Deshaun Watson, who entered the NFL's concussion protocol after reporting concussion symptoms on Tuesday.

Sanders drew attention for the way he handled the press conference in which he fielded questions about the Saints, his recent decision to hire an agent and Watson's performance this season.

When asked if he's had a chance to study the Saints defense, Sanders offered a cryptic answer.

"Yeah, I seen a lot," Sanders said. "When I smile, you know that means – something. I'm maturing, I'm maturing. I could have gave that a decent answer, but now I'm just going to smile whenever it's just like some questions."

Sanders also dismissed a question about his decision to hire an agent, which Shilo called a "setup question."

"What's that have to do with this game?" Shedeur said. "I'm focused on this game. Anything else really doesn't matter at this point."

Shedeur has had a contentious relationship with eporters ever since he was selected in the the fifth round of the 2025 NFL Draft. The second-year quarterback was expected to be a first-round pick before he tumbled down the draft board, and a media frenzy has surrounded the 24-year-old ever since his arrival in Cleveland.

Although Watson has led the Browns to a 5-3 record, Sanders could potentially make a case for the starting position with a strong performance against the struggling Saints defense.

articles.title: Ex-NFL Star Antonio Brown Pleads Guilty to Reduced Charge, Sentenced to Probation in 2025 Shooting
articles.summary: MIAMI (AP) — Former NFL star Antonio Brown pleaded guilty Friday to aggravated assault with a firearm in connection with a 2025 shooting outside a celebrity boxing match in Miami.
articles.body:
MIAMI (AP) — Former NFL star Antonio Brown pleaded guilty Friday to aggravated assault with a firearm in connection with a 2025 shooting outside a celebrity boxing match in Miami.

Judge Marisa Tinkler Mendez sentenced Brown to three years of probation, during which time he will have to attend weekly counseling sessions and not possess a firearm, among other conditions.

Wearing a black leather jacket and white pants, he spoke sparingly and in a low voice during the brief proceedings in Miami state court. As he entered his guilty plea, the judge asked him to speak up.

Outside the courtroom, Brown thanked God and said he wanted to "get back to life" and his family.

He declined to answer other questions, but his lawyer, Mark Eiglarsh, said they were "extremely grateful" the case was behind them.

"My client was facing 30 years in prison with a 20-year minimum mandatory, and he was given an offer he just couldn't refuse," he said. "Probation was too good to turn down, and we're both very excited about the outcome."

The plea to the reduced charge allows the All-Pro wide receiver to avoid prison time and a criminal conviction.

Brown had initially been charged with attempted murder after police say he grabbed a handgun from a security staffer at the event and fired two shots at a man he had been in a fistfight with earlier.

Brown, 38, maintained he was defending himself from an attack as others were trying to steal jewelry from him.

Florida's Stand Your Ground law allows people who believe they face death or serious injury to use deadly force to defend themselves without a duty to retreat.

Prosecutor Howard Rosen said in court Friday that his office was seeking to reduce the charge against Brown because there was "a question" of whether he was actually attempting to shoot the victim, who had been walking away from the altercation at the time.

He noted the victim, who was grazed in the neck, was in court for the hearing and has said publicly that he wouldn't cooperate with police and didn't want to press charges.

"Rather than the entire case going away and there being no opportunity for Mr. Brown to receive what's ultimately going to be some therapeutic treatment, we all came together — the defense and the state — and decided that this was in the best interest of everybody," Rosen said.

The victim, Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu, has said previously that he's since forgiven Brown.

"We are grateful to the Court for ratifying this carefully crafted agreement," Richard Cooper, his lawyer, said in a statement. "We have maintained that we wish Mr. Brown healing and a path closer to God."

Brown spent 12 years in the NFL, most of it with the Pittsburgh Steelers. He won a Super Bowl with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021 under quarterback Tom Brady.

The following season, though, Brown effectively ended his career when he inexplicably took off his jersey, shoulder pads and gloves and ran off the field during a game. The Buccaneers released him after the incident.

Brown has dealt with other legal problems in recent years.

He previously was accused of battery on a moving truck driver , several domestic violence charges, failure to pay child support and other incidents.

Brown was extradited in November 2025 from Dubai , where he has business interests, after an arrest warrant on the attempted murder charge was issued in June of the same year.
authors: Daniel Kozin and Philip Marcelo, Associated Press

articles.title: New Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors Reveal 'Serious Suitor' amid Giants, Vikings, Broncos Links
articles.summary: The trade market for Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor is taking shape as Tuesday's deadline draws closer.
articles.body:
The trade market for Indianapolis Colts star running back Jonathan Taylor is taking shape as Tuesday's deadline draws closer.

According to Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer , the New York Giants are a "serious suitor" for Taylor despite not currently offering a package that the Colts are looking for.

Per Breer, the Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings "might be a little less inclined to trade for Taylor now" after previously discussing swaps with Indianapolis.

The Colts sit at just 2-6 this season and have already started to part ways with multiple key contributors on their roster, trading guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks on Oct. 27 before sending defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers.

Taylor also appears to be available, as ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport previously reported that Indianapolis was "open" to trading the running back.

The Colts reportedly have a high asking price for the three-time Pro Bowler, though.

Per Breer, Indianapolis wants a first-round pick or the "equivalent" of a "Christian McCaffrey–level package" to get a deal done.

The 49ers acquired McCaffrey in exchange for a second-round pick, third-round pick, fourth-round pick and a fifth-rounder in 2022.

Taylor has amassed 610 rush yards this season, ranking No. 8 among all players. He's also found the end zone eight times while averaging 4.1 yards per carry.

The 27-year-old has been extremely productive in recent years, racking up at least 1,500 all-purpose yards and 12 total touchdowns in each of the past two seasons.

The Giants could potentially pair Taylor with Cam Skattebo in their running back room as they look to maintain their lead atop the NFC East standings with a 4-2-1 record.

The 2026 trade deadline is on Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football Bold Predictions
articles.summary: Our Yahoo analysts share their one bold prediction for Week 9 fantasy football.
articles.body:
After Week 9, we'll be at the midway point of the 2026 NFL season. With that, will come plenty of time to reflect on how things have gone and what to expect in the second half of the fantasy football season. But for now, we're focusing on what's in front of us. Here are our bold predictions for fantasy in Week 9.

Kyler Murray isn't a fit for the Vikings' passing game. He's thrown a slant, dig or post route— the key patterns to access big plays in Kevin O'Connell's offense — on just 10.4% of his throws. Only Bo Nix and Patrick Mahomes throw them at a lower rate among NFL quarterbacks. In a small sample, Carson Wentz is at 17.9% this season and 16% last year, which is closer to what Sam Darnold managed in 2024 (17.8%) and Kirk Cousins did in 2022 and 2023 (15.9%).

It was easy to see this coming, as Murray didn't consistently attack the intermediate middle in Drew Petzing's offense. Wentz isn't anyone's idea of a savior but he can execute the offense and find Jefferson. He can do that in a big way against a Bills defense that allows a ton of production to outside receivers. Jefferson is still as elite as ever. He's incentivized to remind folks of that. The Vikings will be eager to get him the ball after he was clearly frustrated at the end of last week's loss. I expect a squeaky-wheel situation on Monday night. — Matt Harmon

Jonah Coleman took the stage last week, completely taking over the backfield from J.K. Dobbins following the opening quarter. Coleman's 26.8 expected fantasy points was the third highest among RBs in Week 8. Denver has quietly been amazing for fantasy running backs, it's just been split between three players over the past calendar year. With no RJ Harvey, the rookie becomes the trusted back in the passing game while running much more successfully than his veteran counterpart Dobbins.

The rushing defense in Carolina hasn't been horrible since their Week 1 disaster versus Chicago, but it has given up plenty of touchdowns to the position as a bottom-five scoring defense, 12 in seven games to be exact. If we get another Panthers game with Bryce Young running for his life, the touchdown opportunities on the other side can be there just as they were for Josh Jacobs and Bucky Irving the past two weeks. With Coleman's goal-line opportunities being paired with his receiving, he won't even need a huge rushing day to cross 20+ fantasy points for you this week. — Joel Smyth

Rome Odunze posts 90 yards, first TD of the season

Odunze topped 52 yards only once in the first six weeks, while the Bears' passing attack struggled to find its rhythm with Caleb Williams missing three games. That's left Odunze as the WR53 in fantasy points per game, but he's 20th in receiving yards and 32nd in receptions among receivers. His biggest problem at the moment is a lack of touchdowns. After scoring six times in 12 outings last year, Odunze has yet to find the end zone through eight weeks. His 44 targets without a TD are the second most behind only KC Concepcion.

Fortunately, with Williams back under center, Odunze is heating up. The 24-year-old posted 69 yards against the Patriots in Week 7 and 87 yards in a tough matchup with the Seahawks on Monday night. The Bears are 6.5-point favorites this week with a strong implied point total of 27. Though the Bucs defense is giving up the seventh-fewest fantasy points to wideouts, in the last month they've allowed five different receivers to top 85 yards. With the Bears' offense picking up steam, get ready for Odunze to finally make a house call. — Justin Boone

Rice finds end zone again on way to top-16 WR finish

Rashee Rice didn't play a full workload in his return last week, and that's exactly why I'm interested. Coming off a multiweek absence and limited practices, he was on the field for just 57% of the snaps and ran a route on 61% of dropbacks. By all accounts, Kansas City planned it that way.

Even so, Rice walked right back into the top target share on the team. The Chiefs didn't need to see more before making him the focal point again. And how they used him matters, too. Six of his eight targets came on slants or other in-breakers, the same get-it-to-him-and-let-him-run usage Andy Reid has leaned on for years.

That's a problem for the Jets. On throws over the middle of the field, they're in the bottom 12 in YAC allowed per reception and rank 18th in EPA allowed per play. Just last week, Kirk Cousins attacked the middle on 60.9% of his throws against New York, and those attempts produced 187 yards and two touchdowns. With his snaps set to climb, Rice gives us a fringe WR1 result in Week 9. — Chris Allen

Ryan Flournoy is my Week 9 sleeper, and I know Indianapolis isn't exactly a matchup we're looking to attack. The Colts are allowing just 27.4 PPR points per game to wide receivers, sixth-fewest in football. But dig a little deeper. Indianapolis is giving up the fifth-most fantasy points to slot receivers, 12.8 yards per completion, third-most in the NFL, and a 6.1% passing touchdown rate, sixth-highest. That's where I think Flournoy can get home. He's playing more than half his snaps from the slot, and with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens commanding attention, he doesn't need massive volume to produce. Flournoy's already given us 70-plus yards or a touchdown in four straight games. My model has him at WR31, 11 spots ahead of consensus, and Jake Ferguson's ankle injury could create even more opportunities. I'm betting on Flournoy making the most of his chances. Give me five catches, 70-plus yards, a touchdown and a top-20 PPR finish in Week 9. — Ray Garvin

Jadarian Price scores his first touchdown of the season

The ceiling has been capped for Price all season — by injury, by fumbles, by the Seahawks insistence on a backfield split. This is a matchup where two Seahawks backs could be fantasy relevant, as Seattle is favored by 8.5 points with backup QB Drew Lock starting. In the last two games between these teams, Seahawks running backs have carried the ball 38 and 35 times. There's a chance we see the Quinton Nelson acquisition show its full colors here. So even if Zach Charbonnet continues to see most of the work inside the 10-yard line, watch for Price to hit an explosive. — Josh Norris

Devin Singletary tops 100 yards or scores a touchdown

We have to ignore the decals on the Philly helmets and start accepting what this is, an injured and bad football team. The offense has taken much of the blame, but the Eagles also can't stop anything on defense (25th in DVOA run defense, 23rd in DVOA pass defense). Singletary is an ordinary back but likely the last man standing with Cam Skattebo hurt, and the Giants would prefer J.J. McCarthy manage the game, not dominate it — especially if Malik Nabers isn't 100%. Volume hunting is a big part of the fantasy equation, and Singletary is ready to be a volume win in Week 9. He's still lagging as a mid-30s RB in industry ECR, but that should correct in the next few days. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: Minkah Fitzpatrick Responds to Backlash over 'Jets Being Jets' Comment After Loss to Raiders
articles.summary: New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick spoke about the controversy that arose from his "Jets being Jets" comment following Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.
articles.body:
New York Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick spoke about the controversy that arose from his "Jets being Jets" comment following Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders.

Speaking to reporters Thursday, Fitzpatrick explained there was no issue within the Jets' locker room because his teammates knew what he was trying to communicate:

"It hasn't really caused any stir within this locker room. I think that's the most important thing. Everybody within this locker room knew what I was talking about. If you look at the context of what I said, if you look at what I've been saying all season, we've been addressing 'Jets not beating Jets' or 'Jets beating Jets.' Everybody within this locker room knew exactly what I said, what I was trying to communicate. ""It hasn't really caused any stir within this locker room. I think that's the most important thing. Everybody within this locker room knew what I was talking about. If you look at the context of what I said, if you look at what I've been saying all season, we've been addressing 'Jets not beating Jets' or 'Jets beating Jets.' Everybody within this locker room knew exactly what I said, what I was trying to communicate."

In the aftermath of the Jets' loss, Fitzpatrick was discussing what went wrong for the defense when he made the comment.

Fitzpatrick has said he was misquoted and his actual comment was "Jets beating Jets" in reference to their miscues and penalties costing them a win.

Things have been rough for the Jets yet again as they are on pace for their 11th consecutive losing season and 16th consecutive year missing the playoffs.

Head coach Aaron Glenn has spent most of his tenure on the hot seat, though no change is expected to happen during the season. He hasn't helped his cause by appearing to not know certain in-game situations.

Fitzpatrick is in his first season with the Jets after being traded in the offseason. He is very familiar with them from his three years playing for the Miami Dolphins.

Whatever the actual comment Fitzpatrick made, the main point is the Jets did hurt themselves against the Raiders. They allowed 24 points in the second half and committed a third-down penalty on two separate drives that gave Las Vegas an automatic first down. Both drives ended with a Raiders touchdown.

The Jets' defensive miscues offset their best offensive performance of the season with 33 points and 439 total yards. They have lost three straight games and sit at 2-6 going into Sunday's matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium.

articles.title: QB-needy Ravens complete trade with Cardinals for Jacoby Brissett after disheartening 'Thursday Night Football' loss
articles.summary: Baltimore will have a week and a half to prepare Brissett for a potential Week 10 start against the Los Angeles Chargers.
articles.body:
Help is officially on the way for the Baltimore Ravens, who completed their trade with the Arizona Cardinals for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett on Friday, the teams announced .

The Ravens are receiving Brissett, whom the Cardinals benched mid-game last week before Gardner Minshew orchestrated an epic road comeback versus the Dallas Cowboys . Plus, Baltimore is getting a 2027 fifth-round pick from Arizona, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported.

The Cardinals also paid a little more than half of Brissett's remaining 2026 salary to tie off the trade, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Arizona is reportedly gaining a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round selection in the exchange.

News of the deal was first reported earlier this week , but the transaction wasn't finalized before the Ravens' "Thursday Night Football" matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Since Lamar Jackson and his backup, Tyler "Snoop" Huntley, landed on injured reserve — with thumb and turf toe injuries, respectively — Baltimore had to start 25-year-old undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano , who wasn't entirely healthy, either.

Fagnano battled through injury, as evidenced by his heavily wrapped right ankle . The rain in Baltimore certainly didn't make things any easier. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle deployed a large dosage of Wildcat plays. When Fagnano did throw, he practically never pushed the ball downfield, finishing with only 60 yards on 10-of-18 passing. He was picked off twice in a 33-10 Jaguars victory that dropped the Ravens to 4-5 .

Baltimore is in last place in a crowded AFC North that's led by the 6-2 Pittsburgh Steelers and also includes the 5-2 Cincinnati Bengals and 5-3 Cleveland Browns.

The arrival of Brissett will far from guarantee a Ravens bounce-back. While Brissett is a serviceable NFL signal-caller, the journeyman went just 4-16 as the Cardinals' starter, and the last of those wins really belongs to Minshew. The 33-year-old Brissett — who has also started games for the New England Patriots, Indianapolis Colts, Miami Dolphins and Browns — is 23rd among all qualifying NFL passers this season in EPA per dropback (-0.11), according to Next Gen Stats.

Whereas Brissett had his fair share of success going deep last season with the Cardinals, under now-Detroit Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing, he struggled mightily in that department within the system used by first-year Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur. Per Pro Football Focus, Brissett is a mere 5 of 28 on passes traveling at least 20 air yards during the 2026 campaign.

Nevertheless, his experience will be welcomed, especially after Baltimore floundered throughout their embarrassing primetime defeat on Thursday night.

Prior to the execution of the Brissett trade, the Cardinals restructured his contract, turning $2.7 million of his remaining $5.4 million salary into a signing bonus, as reported by ESPN's Field Yates . The Ravens are reportedly due to pay Brissett a base salary of $2.43 million, although he has incentives in his deal that allow him to earn more money.

Baltimore will have a week and a half to prepare Brissett for a potential Week 10 start against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Unfortunately for Jesse Minter's Ravens, they have more issues on their claws than just the QB position. Once a possible Super Bowl contender, Baltimore has dropped four straight games. Although its offense has been hamstrung by a cascade of injuries at the sport's most important spot, its defense hasn't stepped up.

That unit's giving up gobs of second-half points, and now three-time All-Pro safety Kyle Hamilton's status is up in the air after he exited Thursday's game with a hip injury.

articles.title: Myles Garrett Injury Update, Latest on Rams Star's Status vs. Commanders
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett is set to return to the lineup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams superstar pass-rusher Myles Garrett is set to return to the lineup against the Washington Commanders on Sunday.

Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters Garrett is expected to play on Sunday after NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported Garrett was "on track to be activated" after practicing all week.

Garrett was not listed with an injury designation despite not taking part in Friday's practice, per the Rams' injury report.

Garrett has not played since Week 1, as he underwent arthroscopic knee surgery and was placed on injured reserve following the Rams' season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

L.A. made the blockbuster trade of the offseason when it acquired Garrett from the Cleveland Browns in exchange for pass-rusher Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, and 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick.

A seven-time Pro Bowler, five-time First Team All-Pro and two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Garrett was coming off the best season of his career.

The 30-year-old veteran set the single-season NFL sack record in 2025 with 23, and the Rams likely assumed they would get something resembling that level of production out of him.

However, Garrett did not look himself in Week 1 after battling a knee injury during training camp and the preseason, and the decision was made for him to undergo surgery and heal up.

Given that the Rams entered the season as the clear Super Bowl favorites, the 2026 campaign has been largely disappointing thus far.

Los Angeles has a 4-4 record, placing it third in the NFC West, and it would not be a playoff team if the season ended today.

Garrett could give the defense a significant lift if he is fully healthy and back to his usual form, though, which is ideal with winnable games on tap against the Commanders and Arizona Cardinals the next two week.

The schedule gets tougher after that with games against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and 49ers, and the Rams' likely hope by that point is that Garrett will have knocked off the rust and be positioned to contribute in a major way.

articles.title: Foye Oluokun Says Jaguars Can't Let Wins 'Mask Stuff,' Team Needs to Improve After Win vs. Ravens
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars improved to 6-2 after trouncing the Baltimore Ravens in a 33-10 victory on Thursday Night Football.
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars improved to 6-2 after trouncing the Baltimore Ravens in a 33-10 victory on Thursday Night Football.

The Jaguars hold a comfortable lead in the AFC South and look primed for another division title, but Jaguars linebacker Foye Oluokun doesn't want the team to rest on their laurels.

"You win and it feels great," Oluokun told reporters . "We can't let wins mask stuff. You've always got stuff to improve. I've been here a while, went through winning, winning, winning, and one season, we let a lot slide because we were winning. So we got to keep learning in wins and stuff because it's all about who's playing the best in December and then we make that run [in] January and February. We got to keep improving all the way through the year, get the advantageous situation going into the playoffs."

The most advantageous situation in the playoffs would be the No. 1 seed in the conference, which would award Jacksonville with a first-round bye and home-field advantage throughout the postseason.

Jacksonville currently holds the No. 3 seed in the AFC, behind only the Denver Broncos and Buffalo Bills. Denver holds the head-to-head tiebreaker against the Jaguars due to Jacksonville's 20-13 loss at Mile High Stadium in Week 2.

The Jaguars have enjoyed success under second-year head coach Liam Coen, but Oluokun has been in Jacksonville long enough to remember the lean years. The veteran linebacker is in his ninth NFL season, five of which he has spent in Jacksonville.

The year the Jaguars "let a lot slide" was likely during the 2023 season. Jacksonville began that campaign with an 8-3 record, but the team collapsed in December and lost five of its final six games. The Jaguars missed the playoffs and fired head coach Doug Pederson after the disappointing finish.

Oluokun finished Thursday night's game with a team-high seven tackles to go along with a sack and a tackle for loss. He currently leads the team with 58 combined tackles, which puts him on pace to surpass 100 tackles for the seventh consecutive season.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Named Browns' QB1 vs. Saints amid Deshaun Watson's Concussion Recovery
articles.summary: With Deshaun Watson still in concussion protocol, Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the 2026 season in Week 9 for the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
With Deshaun Watson still in concussion protocol, Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the 2026 season in Week 9 for the Cleveland Browns.

Browns head coach Todd Monken announced on Friday that Sanders will start against the New Orleans Saints.

Monken added Watson has not yet been ruled out and will be listed as questionable as he goes through the protocol.

Monken expressed confidence in Sanders because of the changes he has seen from him over the course of this season:

"Where he's improved is his footwork, his drops, his mechanics, understanding where to go with the ball, sense of urgency in terms of working through his progressions, protections. There were so many things he needed to work on, and he's done that like any young player. Any young player has a lot to work on, especially at the quarterback position. And you can see that from the moment we got here and that's why we opened up the competition and we split the reps was because of his ascent."

The Browns announced on Wednesday that Watson had been placed in concussion protocol stemming from a helmet-to-helmet hit he took in the first quarter of their Week 8 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Cleveland's statement noted Watson was cleared during the game by the unaffiliated neurotrauma consultants. He was also evaluated by the team's medical staff postgame and on Monday, showed no symptoms and passed his testing.

It was on Tuesday morning Watson reported to the Browns' medical staff he was experiencing concussion symptoms.

NFL rules require players in the protocol to go through a five-step process before they can be cleared to play. Clearance must also occur the day before gameday, so Watson has to pass his tests on Saturday to be available as a backup option.

Sanders has been taking the starting reps in practice this week with Watson unavailable. He has played a total of five offensive snaps in two games this season, including four against the Steelers.

A fifth-round pick in the 2025 draft, Sanders made seven starts as a rookie. He threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, 10 interceptions and completed 56.6 percent of his attempts in eight appearances last season.

The Browns have been a pleasant surprise so far with a 5-3 record. They are tied with the New England Patriots for the final playoff spot in the AFC going into Week 9.

articles.title: New England Patriots player hospitalized with ‘unexplainable’ neurological ailment
articles.summary: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson said he recently experienced an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency.”
articles.body: New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson recently experienced an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency” that required hospitalization, he said in a statement posted to social media on Friday. The second-year player out of Ohio State said the cause of his illness remains a mystery but there has been positive news following diagnostic screenings. He said his yet-to-be-diagnosed issues involved “a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days.” He continued, “During that time, I underwent extensive medical testing and evaluation. While the results of my comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, the cause of this remains unknown and unexplainable.” The 24-year-old added that the medical condition has impacted his physical functions. “I will continue working closely with specialists and physical therapists to focus on my recovery, as these symptoms have affected my strength, coordination, and some of my physical functions. “I am committed to doing everything necessary to return to full health. My health and long-term well-being remain my foremost priorities.” The running back has played in six games so far this season. He has rushed for 203 yards on 52 carries with one touchdown across these games. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel addressed the situation at a press conference on Friday and confirmed that Henderson would not play in Sunday’s game against the Green Bay Packers but said the team would “care for him, listen to him and do whatever we can to get [him] healthy and get back and help this football team and do what he loves.” Vrabel said, “I know that he is well-loved and respected on our football team. My support shows up in a lot of different ways. I’m just trying to make sure that he’s cared for and that the recovery plan is intact and he’s comfortable with it and that his wife Kenzie is cared for.” Vrabel added that it wouldn’t be fair to set a timeline for Henderson’s absence. He missed last week’s game with what the Patriots described as “illness,” and has not participated in team practices this week for the same reason. In six games this season, some of which have been limited by an ankle injury, Henderson has 203 rushing yards and one touchdown. He also has five catches for 45 yards for the 5-3 Patriots. Henderson led the team in rushing last year while appearing in all 17 of New England’s regular season games as well as all four of their postseason games during the Patriots’ run to the Super Bowl, where they lost to the Seattle Seahawks.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Tony Pollard, Calvin Ridley's Value in Titans' Deadline Talks
articles.summary: The Tennessee Titans could be eyeing a further roster shakeup amid a 1-7 start to the season. With the NFL's trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, Nov. 10, Tennessee may be looking to compile more draft picks with a few more trades.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans could be eyeing a further roster shakeup amid a 1-7 start to the season. With the NFL's trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, Nov. 10, Tennessee may be looking to compile more draft picks with a few more trades.

The Titans have been open to trading running back Tony Pollard and wide receiver Calvin Ridley, according to Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer .

"They have listened on both players," Breer wrote on Friday. "Pollard has drawn interest from teams looking for running back help that don't want to pay the freight for [Jonathan] Taylor, and the feeling from those teams is that it would cost at least a fourth-round pick to pry the veteran back from Tennessee. Ridley, who's not playing a ton anymore with Carnell Tate having emerged as the top guy in a fleet of promising young receivers, would come cheaper, maybe for a sixth-rounder or so."

Pollard has rushed for 595 yards and six touchdowns through eight games this season, putting him on pace for his fifth-consecutive 1,000-yard campaign. There are several teams in playoff contention who could use an upgrade at the running back position — particularly the Denver Broncos, Minnesota Vikings, Cincinnati Bengals and Green Bay Packers. All four of those teams currently hold a playoff seed despite ranking bottom-third in rushing yards this season.

Ridley appeared poised to be Tennessee's No. 1 wide receiver after reeling in 76 catches for 1,016 yards in 2024, which was his first season with the team. Since then, his production has dipped. The 32-year-old wide receiver has only been targeted 13 times in seven games this season. Although he's getting older, he could still provide an upgrade for receiver-needy teams like the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Titans made it clear that they're open to trading away their best players ahead of the NFL's trade deadline with the blockbuster deal that saw defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons shipped to the Chicago Bears. Tennessee now holds two first-round picks in each of the next two NFL drafts.

articles.title: NFL Madrid: Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor on Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Bijan Robinson
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals head coach Zac Taylor speaks to Sky Sports NFL as his side prepare to take on the Atlanta Falcons at Real Madrid's Santiago Bernabeu Stadium, live on Sky Sports NFL from 2pm on Sunday.
articles.body:
Joe Burrow arrives in Spain as an MVP frontrunner across the first half of the season as his 5-2 Bengals prepare to face the Atlanta Falcons at the Santiago Bernanbeu on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

Burrow holds a league-high completion percentage of 73 while throwing for 2,115 yards and a league-leading 20 touchdowns to just six interceptions, his 302.1 yards per game also topping all quarterbacks in the NFL.

Cincinnati's poster boy comes into Europe playing some of the football of his life.

"His consistency, and he never wastes a second trying to get himself better," said Taylor, speaking exclusively to Sky Sports, of what makes Burrow special.

"Whether it's his footwork, his placement, reading the body language of the receiver, studying the defense he's going against. He's unbelievable, and he's playing at a high level this year. We're hoping to get that going again on Sunday."

Taylor added in Friday's press conference that Burrow was "arguably the best passer in the world right now".

Between Burrow and a wide receiver tandem of Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase, the Bengals threaten a three-headed monster rivalled by few in the league.

Higgins ranks second in the NFL with 726 receiving yards while Chase has 492 yards, both from 61 targets apiece as two No 1 receivers thriving on the same offense. Together they spearhead the top passing attack in football.

"To have them both on the same team is pretty luxurious for us," said Taylor. "And to be able to put them on the same side, different sides, if defenses are gonna single one of them usually there's great opportunities there for those guys behind them.

"They both have great attention to detail, so we're able to move them around."

On the other side of the ball the Bengals are seeking improvement to a defense that has hindered their Championship credentials in recent seasons.

They sought to addressing as much during the offseason by trading for former New York Giants defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence.

"We got a lot of guys up front that are really talented, Dexter certainly helps us lead the play there," Taylor said.

"He can defend the run and the pass. Teams really have to have a great plan for him in the run and pass game, so he's been a great addition for a lot of things."

Among his prime tasks on Sunday will be slowing down Falcons running back Bijan Robinson, who leads the NFL with 780 rushing yards this season but is without a 100-yard game in Atlanta's last four matchups.

Slowing Robinson is half the battle, such is the foundation he forms for everything Kevin Stefanski wants his offense to be.

"The running back (Robinson) stands out," said Taylor. "He's arguably the best one in the league. You gotta have a great plan. He can go off real quick and then all the things they build off that, the play action, the naked bootlegs, the screens.

"Great on defense, quarterback is great. They do a really good job on that scheme, playing together. And it's gonna make it difficult."

Bengals quarterback Burrow championed the opportunity to play abroad as he explained how this Sunday's game was helping him fulfil a long-term travel dream.

"It means a lot to me that we're here. This is Year 7 for me, and I haven't been overseas yet and we keep adding more and more games to try and build the NFL globally. I think it's worked over the last five years and hoping to add more and continue to build. I love being a part of that and want to help grow the game."

"This is somewhere I've always wanted to go, and so to be able to do it while doing what I love, playing football, really is a dream come true," Burrow said.

Burrow told reporters how he spent time visiting Museo del Prado on Wednesday, with a view to seeing another museum or two and an art gallery before Sunday's game.

Such is the way of an NFL superstar, however, that flying in the radar tends not to be easy, even on European soil

"I ran into some students studying abroad from the United States the other day when I was walking around, that was certainly surprising," Burrow said.

"It's often a little more than I expect when I'm in a different country, I usually expect to go pretty incognito and not have anybody recognise me, it's a little more than that. But I love being out here because I can feel like a normal person a little bit."

articles.title: Antonio Brown: Ex-NFL wide receiver avoids prison after pleading guilty to aggravated assault with a firearm
articles.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers, New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Antonio Brown could have faced up to 30 years in prison if convicted of the original attempted murder charge; Brown, 38, says he wants to "get back to life" and his family
articles.body:
Judge Marisa Tinkler Mendez sentenced the 38-year-old to three years of probation, during which time he will have to attend weekly counselling sessions and not possess a firearm, among other conditions.

Speaking outside the court, Brown said he wanted to "get back to life" and his family.

His lawyer, Mark Eiglarsh, said: "My client was facing 30 years in prison with a 20-year minimum mandatory, and he was given an offer he just couldn't refuse. Probation was too good to turn down, and we're both very excited about the outcome."

The plea to the reduced charge means the All-Pro wide receiver - who played for the Pittsburgh Steelers from 2010-2018 before spells with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he won the Super Bowl in 2021, and the New England Patriots - has avoided a criminal conviction.

He had had initially been charged with attempted murder after police say he grabbed a handgun from a member of security at the boxing event and fired two shots at a man he had been in a fistfight with earlier.

Brown insisted he was defending himself from an attack as others were trying to steal jewellery from him.

Florida's Stand Your Ground law allows people who believe they face death or serious injury to use deadly force to defend themselves without a duty to retreat.

Prosecutor Howard Rosen said his office was seeking to reduce the charge against Brown because there was "a question" of whether he was actually attempting to shoot the victim, who had been walking away from the altercation at the time.

He noted the victim Zul-Qarnain Kwame Nantambu, who was grazed in the neck, was in court for the hearing and has said publicly that he did not want to press charges.

Rosen said: "Rather than the entire case going away and there being no opportunity for Mr Brown to receive what's ultimately going to be therapeutic treatment, we all came together - the defense and the state - and decided this was in the best interest of everybody."

The victim's lawyer, Richard Cooper, said in a statement: "We are grateful to the court for ratifying this carefully crafted agreement. We have maintained we wish Mr Brown healing."

With Rob Gronkowski going into the New England Patriots Hall of Fame this weekend, Dunkin' is getting into the spirit by honoring the legendary tight end in its own way.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Responds to 'Absolutely Ridiculous' Criticism Over HC Salary Comments
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones reacted to criticism surrounding his comments regarding head coaching salaries.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones reacted to criticism surrounding his comments regarding head coaching salaries.

"The facts are I have been out there, and I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on and knew full well that I was going to pay them for their success," Jones said Friday, per ESPN's Todd Archer . "So that has been done. No one knows that, but I do. And so it is absolutely ridiculous. And I actually grin when somebody says, 'Jerry's not willing to pay the money for what it would take to get the right kind of coach out there.'"

Jones came under fire for expressing his belief that a higher head coaching salary doesn't result in more success for the team on Tuesday.

"There's zero correlation between how much you pay a coach or how many coaches you have, as to winning. There's no correlation," Jones said during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan.

Archer reported Friday that Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer is "believed to be in the bottom half of the league in terms of salary." Mike McCarthy, Dallas' head coach before Schottenheimer, was earning $8 million per year.

According to Sportico's Kurt Badenhausen , there are estimated to be 15 current NFL head coaches making at least $12 million per year. Schottenheimer is not among them.

The Cowboys have gone 10-14-1 across Schottenheimer's two seasons patrolling the sidelines after posting a 49-35 record during McCarthy's tenure.

This year, Dallas sits at No. 2 in the NFC East standings with a 3-5 mark.

Rice has disputed the allegations. These legal matters have added another layer to the financial challenges outlined in his bankruptcy filing.Rice entered the NFL in 2023 after being selected by the Kansas City Chiefs in the second round of the draft. He signed a four-year rookie contract worth approximately $6.5 million. He quickly became an important part of the Chiefs' receiving group, helping the franchise win Super Bowl LVIII during his rookie season.However, his career has also been marked by injuries, suspensions and legal controversies. His reported bankruptcy filing now adds another unexpected chapter to his NFL journey.While the $13,640 checking-account figure is certainly attention-grabbing, it is worth remembering that bankruptcy filings provide a snapshot of a person's reported finances at a particular moment. They do not necessarily tell the complete story of their long-term financial position. For Rice, the focus has now shifted from his performances on the field to the millions of dollars in liabilities reportedly outlined in his court documents.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2021, Josh Allen bought land in Orchard Park; his New York mansion and California farm show his life beyond the NFL
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has a life that connects two very different places, California and New York.
articles.body: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has a life that connects two very different places, California and New York. While he spends most of the NFL season in Buffalo, his story began on a family farm in Firebaugh, California. From working in cotton fields as a child to owning a $7.2 million house in Dana Point, Allen’s journey offers an interesting look at his life away from football.Where did Josh Allen grow up and how big is his family farm in California?Josh Allen was born on May 21, 1996, in Firebaugh, California, a small farming town in the state’s Central Valley, around 40 miles west of Fresno. He grew up there with his parents, Joel and Lavonne Allen, and his three siblings. Long before he became the face of the Buffalo Bills, his everyday life involved helping his family with agricultural work.Farming was not a new business for the Allens. His father, Joel, comes from a long line of farmers, and the family has been connected to the agricultural community for generations. According to a 2021 report by the Los Angeles Times, the extended Allen family owned around 1,200 acres of farmland in the Firebaugh area.The land has played an important role in shaping Josh’s childhood. During summer breaks, he often worked alongside his younger brother instead of spending all his time playing sports. His responsibilities included pulling weeds, digging ditches, moving irrigation pipes and helping with cotton fields.The Los Angeles Times reported that Allen also drove tractors while working on the farm. These were not occasional visits to a family property. He was expected to help with the regular work, just like other members of the family.His childhood in Firebaugh also gave him a close connection to the local community. His father once described the town to the Los Angeles Times by saying, “Our community, it’s a pretty special place. We kind of take care of each other.”That connection has remained important even after Allen moved away to build his football career.What does Josh Allen’s family farm grow and how is it connected to Buffalo?The Allen family has continued its farming business even as Josh’s NFL career has grown. Cantaloupes have been one of its main products, with the family also working on expanding its agricultural operation through pistachio farming.In an August 2025 report by The Westside Express, Joel Allen explained that the family had started Allen Family Orchards in 2021. At the time, the operation covered around 600 acres, with plans to add more land and eventually reach 1,000 acres.Pistachios have also become an important part of the family’s plans. The 2025 report explained that the family expected 2026 to be its first major production year for the crop. Josh has also been involved in promoting pistachios through a partnership with Wonderful Pistachios.However, the family’s farming connection is no longer limited to California. In September 2026, Joel and Lavonne brought their agricultural business to Western New York through a partnership with Tops Friendly Markets.According to WGRZ, the JA17 Allen Family Farms cantaloupes returned to participating Tops stores, giving Buffalo residents an opportunity to buy products grown by the quarterback’s family. The family also introduced merchandise, including T-shirts, hats, mugs and tote bags.There was a community reason behind the project as well. A portion of the proceeds from the melon sales and merchandise was set to support the Patricia Allen Fund at Golisano Children’s Hospital of Buffalo.Joel explained that the family wanted to use the partnership to support a community that had welcomed their son. His mother, Lavonne, also described Buffalo as a second home for the family.For Allen, this connection brings together the two places that have played major roles in his life. His family continues to work in California, while their products have found a place among Bills supporters in New York.Where Does Josh Allen Live in Buffalo and What Does His Orchard Park Mansion Look Like?California may be where Josh Allen grew up, but Buffalo has become his professional home. The quarterback joined the Bills in 2018 after being selected seventh overall in the NFL Draft. Since then, he has made the Buffalo area an important part of his life.Allen owns property in Orchard Park, a suburb of Buffalo where the Bills’ stadium and training facilities are located. According to Realtor.com, he purchased land in the area in 2021 for around $500,000 and later had a custom-built mansion developed there.The property sits on approximately 31 acres, giving Allen plenty of private space away from the attention that comes with being an NFL star. Its location is also convenient for his football commitments, as it is around eight minutes from Highmark Stadium.The Orchard Park estate has several features that make it stand out. Reports describe a large swimming pool, a separate pool house and a private sports court that can be used for basketball and tennis. The property also has a private par-3 golf hole, giving Allen another way to enjoy his time away from football.His connection to Orchard Park goes beyond owning an expensive property. Living close to the Bills’ facilities allows him to remain connected to the team throughout the season without having to travel far for practices and other commitments.According to Mansion Global, Allen also owns two homes in Orchard Park. However, detailed information about the interiors and current arrangements of his private residences has not been publicly confirmed.Unlike his California property, which has been listed for sale, there has been no comparable confirmed announcement that he is selling his Orchard Park estate.Does Josh Allen own a $7.2 million house in Dana Point, California?Apart from his property in New York, Josh Allen also has a connection to Southern California through his Dana Point house. He purchased the property in 2023 for $7.2 million, according to Mansion Global. The house is located in Monarch Bay, a gated coastal community in Orange County.The property covers approximately 2,808 square feet and has four bedrooms and three bathrooms. Built in 1962, it features a single-level design with mid-century architecture. The house also has large windows and sliding glass doors that connect the indoor living areas to the backyard.The main living space includes a family room with high ceilings, a formal dining area and a kitchen with quartz countertops. The primary bedroom has a separate sitting area, while the backyard offers outdoor space, a hot tub and patio areas.Another attraction is the location. The property is around half a mile from the beach, and residents of Monarch Bay have access to the private Monarch Bay Beach Club.Allen’s plans for the house changed after his purchase. In July 2025, he reportedly put the property on the market for $8.5 million. However, it was taken off the market in January 2026.The quarterback made another attempt to sell it in September 2026, this time with a reduced asking price of $7.95 million. Realtor.com reported the new listing on September 14, while Mansion Global also covered his second attempt to sell the property.The decision to list the Dana Point house does not mean Allen has lost his connection to California. He was born and raised in the state, and his parents and family farming business remain based there.His property choices reflect the different parts of his life. Orchard Park keeps him close to his NFL career, while Dana Point offered a place to enjoy California’s warmer weather during the offseason. Firebaugh, meanwhile, remains the place where his family’s story began.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kylie Kelce opens up about unexpected struggles her family is facing in public
articles.summary: Kylie Kelce is opening up about one of the unexpected challenges of being part of one of America's most recognizable football families, and it involves
articles.body: Kylie Kelce is opening up about one of the unexpected challenges of being part of one of America's most recognizable football families, and it involves her four young daughters. Being connected to the Kelce family comes with plenty of attention, especially after Travis Kelce's relationship with Taylor Swift brought an entirely new audience into their lives. But while fans may be excited to spot someone from the famous family, Kylie is making it clear that there is a difference between showing support and crossing personal boundaries.Kylie Kelce raises concerns over overexcited fans as she reveals uncomfortable encounters involving her four daughtersDuring the latest episode of her podcast, Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce, the mother of four sat down with HGTV star Joanna Gaines and discussed what it is like raising children while living in the public eye.Kylie, who shares four daughters with her husband Jason Kelce, explained that she does not want fame to become a reason for keeping her children away from everyday experiences."I always say, like, we're not gonna hole up in our house and keep our kids hidden. We're not hermits," she said.However, she admitted that navigating public interactions with young children can sometimes become difficult. Kylie explained that people can get so excited when they recognize someone from the Kelce family that they forget basic social etiquette."I think people sort of lose sight and their excitement overrides social etiquette or proper social behavior," she explained.She added that adults might get caught up in the excitement of recognizing someone, without considering that the person they are approaching could simply be a five-year-old child.Taylor Swift's connection brings even more attention to the Kelce familyIt is hardly surprising that the Kelce family attracts plenty of attention. Jason's successful NFL career and Travis' popularity with the Kansas City Chiefs already made the family recognizable to football fans. However, Travis' relationship with global pop superstar Taylor Swift introduced the family to an entirely different audience.Swifties have become familiar with several members of the Kelce family, including Kylie, who has also developed her own public profile through her podcast and appearances. That increased visibility makes Kylie's comments about personal boundaries particularly relevant. While fans may feel connected to celebrities and their families, that connection does not automatically extend to their children.Kylie is not suggesting that her daughters should grow up hidden away from the world. Instead, she wants them to enjoy ordinary childhood experiences without having to navigate uncomfortable attention from strangers. And that might be one of the biggest challenges of raising children in a family that has become so famous.Jason and Kylie Kelce prepare their daughters for encounters with strangersThe podcast host also shared the important lesson she regularly teaches her older daughters before they head out in public. Kylie revealed that whenever the family gets out of the car to go somewhere, she reminds her children that recognizing someone does not mean they actually know them."Just because someone knows mom's name does not mean that mom knows them," she tells her daughters.She also explains that even if someone calls them by their names, it does not necessarily mean they know that person. Kylie said she feels the need to prepare her seven-, five- and three-year-old daughters for adults who sometimes struggle to maintain appropriate social boundaries.Her approach is about helping her children understand these unexpected interactions without making them feel that they need to avoid the outside world.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, and his brother, the former player Jason Kelce, have both remained close to their mother, Donna Kelce, as they have achieved remarkable success on the field. While Donna Kelce has been a pretty protective mother, she has opened up about her feelings when she watches them play.Travis Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce reflects on her feelings as she watched her sons play for over a decadeIn an interview for Mashed, Travis Kelce’s mother said, “No, I really do enjoy football. I can honestly say that I'm a true fan and I can compartmentalize. I can pull myself out, [and] not even think about my kids being out there.”The Traitors star added, “Half the time, I'm not looking at them unless they get the ball thrown to them, and I don't follow them all around the field. I just look at the whole game and I really enjoy it.”Travis Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce also reflected on the rituals they have at home when either of her sons played in the Super Bowl as she said, “[For the Super Bowl], you just have to ask. You have to know your room. If there are kids there, you're going to have chicken nuggets. articles.title: Giants reportedly 'aggressive' in pursuit of help at one position, and it's not RB
articles.summary: The Giants are making a serious push to get a big addition at this position.
articles.body:
The New York Giants are 4-2-1 heading into their Week 9 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles . With a win, the Giants could extend their NFC East lead and further be convinced to be big spenders at the NFL trade deadline.

Currently, they're trending towards buying, with a few positions emerging as potential areas to upgrade. While they might buy, how aggressive will this Giants team actually be in the trade market?

According to NFL insider James Palmer , the Giants have been "very aggressive" in pursuit of one position in trade talks. But, it's not running back for someone like Jonathan Taylor, it's along the defensive line.

Giants have been 'aggressive' in pursuit of DL help

"The Giants are another team to keep an eye on. They have been very aggressive, just like Jacksonville on that defensive front," Palmer said. "There have been some names contacted around the NFL... that I didn't expect teams would be reaching out about because they're borderline untouchable."

This report from Palmer indicates that the Giants are going to make a real push to land a star defensive lineman this season. There are a few names that stand out.

While Moro Ojomo of the Philadelphia Eagles probably isn't realistic, with the Eagles not being likely to trade him in-division, someone like Derrick Brown of the Carolina Panthers or Vita Vea of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers could be in play.

More realistically, though, the Giants could look to acquire Grover Stewart from the Indianapolis Colts . Nnamdi Madibuike from the Baltimore Ravens , if they decide to sell, could be a fun option as well.

New England Patriots defensive tackle Christian Barmore would make plenty of sense, and there are other options like Bobby Brown III of the Panthers and New Orleans Saints ' DTs Davon Godchaux and Nathan Shepherd that are worth considering.

John Harbaugh and the Giants already tried making a push for Jeffery Simmons before he was dealt to the Chicago Bears .

They are willing to spend big on a top lineman, even though they might not be as good as their 4-2-1 record might indicate.

While they might still be in the market for running back help, and another position or two could make sense, defensive lineman has become a position to watch for the Giants at the 2026 NFL trade deadline.

articles.title: Eagles receive Saquon Barkley boost ahead of Giants game
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles receive an encouraging Saquon Barkley update as they prepare for their Week 9 showdown with the New York Giants.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are preparing for an important NFC East matchup against the New York Giants in NFL Week 9. Saquon Barkley 's fitness has been a concern after the running back dealt with hamstring and back issues.

His availability could be important to Philadelphia's offensive plans, especially after the team managed his workload in its previous game. However, the latest development offers the Eagles encouragement heading into Sunday's contest.

Saquon Barkley listed as limited participant

The Eagles listed Barkley as a limited participant on Thursday's injury report after he missed Wednesday's session. He was listed with hamstring and back injuries, marking a positive step in his recovery.

Barkley battled through those issues during Philadelphia's Week 8 matchup against the Washington Commanders, scoring a touchdown despite his fitness concerns. However, Elijah Mitchell took on a larger share of the backfield work.

The Eagles will continue to monitor his condition as they complete their preparations. A full return to practice would provide further encouragement, but Thursday's update is already a welcome development for the team.

Barkley's availability is important for an Eagles offense that ranks 29th in rushing yards. He leads the team with 274 rushing yards and averages 4.9 yards per carry, making his return valuable as Philadelphia looks to end its six-game losing streak.

The Eagles host the Giants on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: ESPN says Giants should target Falcons DT at NFL trade deadline
articles.summary: ESPN lists Falcons DT Maason Smith as trade deadline target for NFC East team
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons are likely approaching the 2026 NFL trade deadline with an open mind. After all, the team is just 3-5 and unlikely to shake up the roster. However, the Falcons do play in the NFC South - the league's least-serous division - and aren't even close to being out of the playoff hunt.

While we could definitely envision general manager Ian Cunningham using the deadline to upgrade a position or two, we don't see any reason why he would ship off valuable contributors unless the offer was just too good to refuse.

Nonetheless, the NFL trade deadline always creates rampant speculation around the league. In a recent ESPN trade feature, Seth Walder made a case for the New York Giants to target Falcons defensive tackle Maason Smith before the deadline.

"Falcons DT Maason Smith. The Falcons are suddenly somewhat loaded at defensive tackle. The stats paint a bit of a mixed picture on Smith, who ranks in the 96th percentile in pass rush win rate and 38th percentile in pressure rate. But the Giants could use an interior player who could provide some pass rushing threat in passing situations, and Smith could be that." - Seth Walder, ESPN

Smith has been a quality addition thus far, and since the Falcons traded former second-round pick Ruke Orhorhoro to acquire him from Jacksonville, we don't see the upside in the move. Of course, if the price was right, all bets are off.

The Falcons have a few minor needs and could use some extra wide receiver depth. Rookie Zachariah Branch was ruled out back on Monday, which could be an indication that his hamstring injury is slightly more severe than we thought.

ESPN also listed Falcons cornerback Mike Hughes as a trade target for the Detroit Lions . Plus another recent ESPN feature suggested Atlanta trade for Houston Texans wide receiver Kayshon Boutte .

Some of this could depend on how the team fares in this Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain. The NFL trade deadline is on Tuesday at 4 p.m. ET.
